title: Voice dictation for Claude Code: how to talk to your terminal in 2026
summary: How to turn on Claude Code's /voice dictation, fix it when it fails, and dictate to Claude Code from every other app too.
body_markdown:
**Yes, Claude Code has a built-in voice mode.** Run` /voice` in the CLI, hold Space, speak, and release: your words land in the prompt, tuned for coding terms. It needs a Claude.ai login and a local microphone. To dictate the same way in Cursor, your terminal, GitHub, and Slack, add a system-wide dictation app like Aqua.


Here's how to set up Claude Code voice mode, how to fix it when it won't start, where it stops, and how to dictate to Claude Code when the built-in isn't available.


## How to turn on Claude Code voice mode


Claude Code's voice dictation is the zero-setup path. Per the[Claude Code voice dictation docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/voice-dictation) :


1. **Update Claude Code** to the latest version and sign in with a Claude.ai account (` /login` ).
2. **Run` /voice`** in the CLI. Claude Code runs a microphone check; on macOS the first run triggers the system microphone permission prompt for your terminal.
3. **Hold Space, talk, release.** Your speech streams into the prompt dimmed, then commits at your cursor when you let go. Press Enter to send.


That's hold mode, the default.` /voice` also takes a mode argument:


Command


What it does


` /voice`


Toggle voice on or off, keeping the current mode


` /voice hold`


Push-to-talk: record while Space is held


` /voice tap`


Tap Space to start, tap again to stop and send


` /voice off`


Turn voice dictation off


Voice stays enabled across sessions. You can also set it in your settings file with a` voice` object (` "enabled": true` ,` "mode": "tap"` ).


### Hold mode vs tap mode


**Hold mode** detects a held Space through your terminal's key-repeat, so there's a brief warmup (the footer shows` keep holding…` , then` listening…` ). A single tap still types a space. By default the transcript waits for Enter; set` "autoSubmit": true` in the` voice` settings to send on release when the transcript is at least three words.


**Tap mode** has no warmup. Tap Space on an empty prompt to start (the footer shows` ● REC · tap to send` ), speak, tap again, and Claude Code inserts and submits anything three words or longer. Recording also stops on its own after 15 seconds of silence or two minutes total.


Press **Esc** or **Ctrl+C** to cancel a recording; the prompt goes back to what it held before you started.


### What it's tuned for


Transcription is tuned for code: terms like` regex` ,` OAuth` ,` JSON` , and` localhost` come out right, and **your project name and git branch are added as recognition hints automatically** . It works in the CLI, in Claude Code's VS Code extension, and in agent view, where you can dictate to a background session. Transcription doesn't consume Claude messages or tokens.


### Change the dictation language


Voice dictation follows Claude Code's` language` setting (set it in` /config` ) and defaults to English. Anthropic lists 20 supported dictation languages, including English, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Hindi, and Portuguese. If your language isn't on the list,` /voice` warns you and falls back to English.


### Rebind the dictation key


The key is the` voice:pushToTalk` action in` ~/.claude/keybindings.json` . Binding a modifier combination like` meta+k` skips the hold-mode warmup entirely. Avoid a bare letter key in hold mode, since it types into the prompt during warmup.


## Claude Code voice mode not working? Common fixes


Most failures come down to one of these, per Anthropic's troubleshooting list:


- **"Voice mode requires a Claude.ai account."** You're signed in with an Anthropic API key or a third-party provider. Voice dictation isn't available with an API key directly, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. Run` /login` with a Claude.ai account, or use a system-wide dictation app (below).
- **"Voice mode is disabled by your organization's policy."** An admin has turned it off. Ask your administrator.
- **"Microphone access is denied."** Enable your terminal under System Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Microphone on macOS (or microphone access for desktop apps on Windows), then run` /voice` again. If your terminal isn't listed on macOS, reset its permission with` tccutil reset Microphone` plus your terminal's bundle ID, quit the terminal fully, and run` /voice` again.
- **Holding Space just types spaces.** Voice is probably off (run` /voice hold` ), or your OS has key-repeat disabled, which hold detection relies on. Switch to` /voice tap` .
- **It won't record in a remote session.** Voice needs a local microphone, so it doesn't work in cloud sessions, SSH sessions, or VS Code Remote (SSH, Dev Containers, Codespaces).
- **Garbled text or the wrong language.** Set your dictation language in` /config` first.


## Where the built-in stops


None of this makes the built-in bad. It's genuinely good for dictating a prompt straight into the agent you're already in. It's *scoped* , and three boundaries matter once you live in voice:


- **It only works inside Claude Code.** The CLI, the VS Code extension, and agent view: that's the perimeter. Switch to Cursor's composer, a plain terminal tab, a GitHub PR description, Gmail, Slack, or another agent like Codex, and that microphone is gone.
- **It depends on how you sign in.** API-key, Bedrock, Agent Platform, and Foundry setups don't get it, and an org policy can switch it off. Plenty of professional setups run exactly those paths.
- **20 dictation languages.** Great if you speak one of them; a real limit if you don't. (Aqua supports 49 languages.)


For a single-tool session, the built-in is all you need. For an agent-era workflow that crosses apps all day, you want one voice everywhere.

1. **Install Aqua** on macOS or Windows from[aquavoice.com](https://aquavoice.com/) and grant microphone + accessibility permissions.
2. **Open your terminal** (or the VS Code integrated terminal) where Claude Code runs. Aqua works in any text field, including the CLI prompt, with no Claude.ai login and no provider restrictions.
3. **Hold Fn, dictate your prompt, release.** Your transcript inserts at the cursor in Claude Code's input. Press Enter to send.
4. **Load your stack into the Custom Dictionary:** framework names, services, CLI tools, the libraries you say twenty times a day. See the[setup guide](https://aquavoice.com/guide) .

Building voice into your own agent instead? Avalon is available as an[OpenAI-compatible API](https://aquavoice.com/avalon-api) .


## Tips for dictating prompts to a coding agent


- **Be verbose.** A fast input means you can give the agent the full picture: the file, the constraint, the edge case, the thing you already tried. More signal, better output, and now it costs seconds instead of minutes.
- **Name the casing when it matters.** "camelCase user ID" produces` userId` ; "snake_case max retries" produces` max_retries` .
- **Dictate file paths and flags naturally.** Avalon's training includes them, and Deep Context can often see the path you mean on screen.
- **Mix typing and talking.** Type the half that's faster to type; hold a key and speak the half that's faster to say. Both Aqua and Claude Code's` /voice` insert at your cursor, so you can type around the transcript.

## FAQ


**Does Claude Code have a voice mode?** Yes. Run` /voice` in Claude Code to dictate prompts with push-to-talk: hold Space to record, release to insert.` /voice tap` switches to tap to start, tap to send. It's tuned for coding vocabulary, adds your project and git-branch names as recognition hints, and works in the CLI, the VS Code extension, and agent view.


**Why does Claude Code say "Voice mode requires a Claude.ai account"?** Voice dictation streams audio to Anthropic's transcription service, which is only available when you sign in with a Claude.ai account. It isn't available with an Anthropic API key directly, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. Run` /login` , or use a system-wide dictation app like Aqua, which doesn't depend on how Claude Code is authenticated.


**Do I still need a separate dictation app if Claude Code has` /voice` ?** Only if your workflow leaves Claude Code. Built-in voice works inside Claude Code. If your day also spans Cursor, the terminal, GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, or you run Claude Code through a provider where built-in voice isn't available, a system-wide tool like Aqua gives you one push-to-talk with the same accuracy everywhere.


**Is voice dictation accurate enough for coding?** It is when the model is built for it. Aqua's Avalon model is trained on code and prompt speech and was the #1 proprietary model on the public OpenASR leaderboard at its October 2025 debut, and a custom dictionary handles your repo's specific terms. Claude Code's built-in voice is also coding-tuned and uses your project and branch as hints.


**What languages does Claude Code voice dictation support?** Anthropic lists 20, chosen through Claude Code's` language` setting, with English as the default. Aqua supports 49 languages.
